changelog: fix: the R re-render draws the samples and groups set in the editor — and viz_pipeline.R can finally read the app's metadata at all. (1) viz_pipeline.R read metadata with read.table(sep='\t', quote=''). The app writes metadata.csv, COMMA-separated, so every line came in as one column named after the whole header row ('sampleId.group.description'), the grouping column was never found, and has_meta was FALSE on every run that used the app's own metadata. Fifty-six branches in the script key off has_meta — PCoA by group, alpha by group, group-mean bars — and none of them had ever run for such a job; the only trace was 'has_metadata: FALSE' in the log. quote='' broke it a second way: a description containing a comma, quoted as any CSV writer quotes it, split into two cells. It now sniffs the delimiter, reads with normal quoting, finds the id column by name, and matches the grouping column case-insensitively, falling back to a column called group when the default 'treatment' is absent — which it nearly always is. This affects ordinary runs too, not just re-renders: the by-group R figures will appear from the next run on. (2) The re-render now draws the samples the editor shows: a sample switched off is out, and a sample with no value in the active grouping is not part of that comparison and is out too — so Grouping2, holding R1 and R2, renders two of four. The log names what was left out and why. (3) Re-render in R saves the groups to metadata.csv and the settings (now including the active grouping, the hidden samples and the ungrouped rule) to settings.json BEFORE starting R, in that order, because R reads both files and a grouping that has only been typed is not in either. Previously an unsaved grouping simply never reached R. (4) A re-render into its own folder writes its tables beside its figures, not into r_tables/. Otherwise drawing two of four samples would have rewritten the tables the chart editor reads, and the editor would have shown two samples from then on. The production console reads font, colors, sampleAliases and sampleOrder by name and ignores other keys, so the three new ones do not split settings.json between the consoles. Verified: the metadata block run against the real metadata.csv, a Grouping2 file with blanks and a quoted comma, and a TSV; and 18 drivers, 574 checks.
